findings.title: Secret fields for provider drivers come from a hand-kept list, so a missed driver stays plaintext
findings.body: `providerSecretFields` hard-codes codex, claudeAgent, antigravity, plus six client definitions. `mapSettingsSecrets` looks fields up with `providerSecretFields.get(instance.driver) ?? []`. A provider that later marks a field with `secretSetting`, or a driver not in this list, is neither redacted for clients nor moved to the secret store. Nothing fails; the value is sent to every client and left in settings.json in plaintext. The `secretSetting` annotation is meant to make this schema-driven, but this list still needs an edit for each new driver. Consider deriving the map from the same provider client definitions the web uses, or adding a test that every registered driver's settings schema appears here.

findings.title: Migration and rollback warnings no longer say which secret failed
findings.body: The old warning logged `{kind, field}` for the host secret that could not be moved. The new one, "failed to move a settings secret into the secret store", carries no context and drops the error cause, so an operator cannot tell which of the provider-config, host or quota secrets is stuck. The move is retried on every load, so this warning repeats. Log the secret kind and the `providerInstanceId` / `environmentVariable` metadata (never the value). The rollback warning at line 1006 has the same gap for field secrets, which have no instance id or variable name.

findings.title: Card and dialog variants render a saved secret as the redaction marker
findings.body: In the `card`/`dialog` fallthrough, `SecretInput` receives `value={readProviderConfigString(value, field.key)}` and no `configured`. For a saved secret, the server now sends the marker "••••••" as that value. The input would then show the marker with the "Not set" placeholder. In the controlled branch (`ControlledInput`, no `onCommit`), typing appends to the marker and the resulting "••••••x" would be saved as the secret. The `settings` variant, which every current caller uses (AddProviderInstanceDialog, ProviderInstanceCard, SourceControlHostSettings), handles this correctly with `value=""` and `configured`. These two branches are not reachable today. Either give them the same `configured`/empty-value treatment or drop the secret handling from them.

findings.title: First assertion does not exercise the `configured && next === ""` guard
findings.body: In the first test, `value=""` is passed, so `useCommitOnBlur` (apps/web/src/hooks/useCommitOnBlur.ts:29-34) skips `onCommit` when the draft equals `value` ("" === ""). `expect(onCommit).not.toHaveBeenCalled()` therefore passes even if the guard in SecretInput.tsx:32 is removed. The test name says it preserves a configured secret on empty edits, but the guard is never reached. To cover it, render with a non-empty `value` and `configured`, then edit to "". Note the same reachability point applies to the production callers: ProviderSettingsForm.tsx:422 passes `value=""` and ProviderInstanceCard.tsx:428 passes `""` whenever `valueRedacted` is true, so the guard is never reached with `configured` set there either. It can be dropped, or the test should construct the case where it matters.

contracts.action: Schema-declared secret fields (provider config, host tokens, quota key) are stored in the secret store and redacted for clients through one `mapSettingsSecrets` walk
contracts.equivalent_path: Old per-kind code in serverSettings.ts: provider env, usage-limit and host-slot loops (removed in this diff)
contracts.before_after: Secret names are unchanged for env (`provider-env-<id>-<name>`), hosts (`sourceControlHostSecretName`) and usage-limit (`usage-limit-source-<id>`, no suffix for null serverHost). Provider config secrets get new names (`provider-config-<id>-<driver>-<field>`). Redaction output matches the old rules.
contracts.visible_effect: The Antigravity apiKey is now redacted to the marker for clients; it was previously sent in plaintext.
contracts.failure_mode: A driver whose secret field is not in `providerSecretFields` is left unredacted and unmigrated.

contracts.action: On load, plaintext secret fields are moved into the secret store and settings.json is rewritten with the marker
contracts.equivalent_path: moveInlineSourceControlHostSecrets, which did this for host tokens only
contracts.before_after: The same flow now also covers provider config and the quota key. A failed `secretStore.set` leaves the value in the file and retries on the next load. Only `kind === "field"` secrets are moved; environment variables are not.
contracts.visible_effect: An existing Antigravity apiKey disappears from settings.json after the first start.
contracts.failure_mode: A store failure is only logged as a warning without context. After the rewrite, a downgraded build reads the marker as the real key.

contracts.action: Client redaction of server settings now covers provider config secrets
contracts.equivalent_path: ws.ts RPC and stream handlers that call `redactServerSettingsForClient`
contracts.before_after: The signature is unchanged and the callers are the same. Env, usage-limit and host redaction match the old behavior.
contracts.visible_effect: The client receives the marker for a saved provider config secret. The settings UI treats a non-empty value as "configured".
contracts.failure_mode: An older client talking to a newer server sees the marker as the real key, but only if it round-trips it. The server treats the marker as "keep".

contracts.action: SecretInput wraps DraftInput/Input with the configured placeholder and a guard against committing an empty draft
contracts.before_after: The "Stored secret…" placeholder and the `type=password` / `autoComplete=off` attributes now come from one place. The `settings` variant passes `value=""` and `configured`. `useCommitOnBlur` commits only when the draft differs from `""`.
contracts.visible_effect: The placeholder reads "Stored secret, enter a new value to replace" for configured secrets and the field's own placeholder (or "Not set") otherwise.
contracts.failure_mode: The `card` and `dialog` variants do not pass `configured` and would show the marker (see finding).

contracts.action: `settingsSecret` annotation declared in contracts and read by server persistence/redaction and web form
contracts.equivalent_path: Previously `providerSettingsForm.secret`, read only by `secretSourceControlHostSettingsFields` in source-control-core for source control hosts.
contracts.before_after: Before: a `secret` flag inside the `providerSettingsForm` annotation, honored only for source control hosts. After: a separate `settingsSecret` key annotation, with `secretSettingsFields` shared by the server (settingsSecrets.ts:25-33, sourceControlHostSecrets.ts:34) and `isSecretSetting` used by the web form (ProviderSettingsForm.tsx:136). Annotation lookup is `resolveAnnotationsKey ?? resolveAnnotations`. `annotateKey` merges into the existing context annotations (SchemaAST.ts:4402-4411), and `withDecodingDefault` keeps the inner schema's context (Schema.ts:5911, SchemaAST.ts:4366-4375). So `secretSetting` placed before or after `withDecodingDefault` and followed by `annotateKey` all keep the flag. This holds for gitcafe (before), github (after) and usage-limit managementKey (after).
contracts.visible_effect: Antigravity `apiKey`, usage-limit `managementKey`, and the GitHub/GitCafe/Bitbucket tokens are flagged secret. Server redacts them to clients and stores them separately.
contracts.failure_mode: A secret field that sits after a wrapper which drops key context would silently stay plaintext. The orderings used here keep the flag. Placement is inconsistent between files (before vs after withDecodingDefault) but works.

contracts.before_after: The removed helper had one caller, now replaced by `secretSettingsFields` in sourceControlHostSecrets.ts:34. A repo-wide search finds no remaining reader of `providerSettingsForm.secret` or the removed helper. The `Schema` import is still used in the file.
contracts.visible_effect: No behavior change for source control hosts.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** The refactor to a single `mapSettingsSecrets` walk looks equivalent to the old per-kind code for env, host and quota secrets. It keeps the existing secret names and adds protection for the Antigravity `apiKey`. I found no correctness defects on the paths that are reachable today. Three smaller points: the provider-driver secret list is hand-maintained, the warning logs lost their identifying context, and the unused card/dialog form variants would show the redaction marker for a saved secret. I did not run the tests or the code.

**Batch 2 of 2.** This part moves the secret flag out of `providerSettingsForm` into a separate `settingsSecret` key annotation, with shared helpers `secretSetting`, `isSecretSetting` and `secretSettingsFields`. I found no defects in the contracts or the four source control definitions. The annotation survives `withDecodingDefault` and a later `annotateKey` in every ordering used here, and no reader of the old `providerSettingsForm.secret` flag remains. The one finding is on the new `SecretInput` test: its first assertion passes without the `configured && next === ""` guard it claims to test. That guard is also unreachable from the current callers, which pass an empty `value` whenever the secret is configured.
